key_insight: The paper extends a previously discovered mathematical equivalence between two-dimensional vortical and capillary free-boundary flows to a new pair of problems: a hollow vortex in shear/strain and a surface-tension bubble in straining flow.
engineering_relevance: This analogy can let researchers transfer analytical and numerical tools between seemingly different fluid-interface problems, improving how equilibrium shapes and free boundaries are modeled.
method: Constructed an exact isolated solution for the special case γ = 0.
Computed numerical solutions for non-zero γ to test the extended analogy.
Identified conformal mapping identities that hold for capillary flows and, under parameter constraints, for hollow-vortex flows as well.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports both an exact solution at γ = 0 and numerical solutions for γ ≠ 0, indicating the extension is supported by analytical construction plus computation.
watch_item: The analogy appears to require parameter constraints, so the mapping may not apply broadly without careful checking of each flow configuration.
paper_title: Extension of a mathematical analogy between vortical flows without surface tension and irrotational capillary flows
